groups.title: On the water
groups.desc: The Atlantic is cooling from about 20C, and the lagoon boats are on short winter timetables.

items.name: The sea in late October and November
items.teaser: About 18–20C in November, down from about 21C in October: an Atlantic swim, not a Mediterranean one
items.story: Faro's sea is Atlantic water, and it cools through the autumn. Holiday-weather gives an average of 21C for October falling to 20C in November; other climate guides put mid-November nearer 18 to 19C, with a range of about 18 to 21C. These are long-run averages from travel and forecast sites, not a buoy reading. The ocean beaches of the barrier islands, Ilha de Faro, Deserta, Culatra and Armona, face the open Atlantic. The air drops fast once the sun goes, and from 25 October it goes an hour earlier.
items.why: Swim at midday on a calm day in the sun, and keep a wetsuit aboard for anyone who feels the cold.
facts: Late Oct to end Nov, cooling week by week
Praia de Faro or the barrier islands
Averages only: check a live sea reading before a long swim

items.name: The island boats on winter times
items.teaser: Olhão–Armona runs about four boats a day from October to March; the last boat back leaves around 17:30
items.story: The lagoon ferries shrink after the summer. In October 2024 the posted timetable at Olhão gave only four crossings a day to Armona from October to the end of March, the first at about 08:30, and moved the last boat off the island from 20:00 to about 17:30 after 20 September; an extra 10:00 sailing ran only 'when justified'. No 2026 winter timetable for Armona or Culatra was found, and none for the Animaris boats from Faro to Ilha Deserta, whose booking pages show summer departures. Visit Portugal says Estaminé on Deserta opens daily from April to September and by reservation the rest of the year.
items.why: Ask at the Olhão ticket office the day before, and never plan a lunch that depends on the last boat.

items.name: Teatro das Figuras in November

The Orquestra Sinfónica Portuguesa, under Antonio Pirolli, plays Mil e uma Noites, music of the imagined Orient, on 7 November at 18:30. The punk band The Parkinsons and Sereias play the theatre's new Noites à Margem series on the 13th; the Lisbon Poetry Orchestra opens the tenth Calceteiros de Letras spoken-word festival on the 15th. Olga Roriz's company dances O Mundo Inteiro à Espera on the 21st, and Moby Dick comes from the Contrapeso festival on the 27th.

items.name: Medronho: the picking season
items.teaser: The arbutus berries are picked September to November; the stills run after, January to March
items.story: Medronho, the clear spirit of the Algarve hills, starts now. A documentary on the spirit filmed the picking of the arbutus berries between September and November and the distilling between January and March: the fruit ferments in vats for weeks before it reaches the copper still. In the Serra do Caldeirão the picking is said to end in November. In Marmelete, west of Monchique, the Casa do Medronho runs a Roteiro do Medronho with picking and distilling workshops with local producers. No Festa do Medronho for autumn 2026 was found: Monchique's 2026 town festival with medronho stalls, Vamos à Vila, was in May.
items.why: Buy a bottle from a Monchique producer with a label and a licence, and taste it before the meal, not after.
facts: Spirit distilled from fermented arbutus berries

items.name: São Martinho, Wed 11 November
items.teaser: Roasted chestnuts and the first wine of the year on St Martin's Day; Ferreiras holds its festa from 17:00
items.story: São Martinho, 11 November, is the day of chestnuts and the year's new wine across Portugal; in 2026 it falls on a Wednesday and is not a public holiday. The magusto is a bonfire of roasted chestnuts, and street sellers' smoking carts appear in every town. In the Algarve, the parish of Ferreiras near Albufeira holds its Festa de São Martinho on the Largo da Nora from 17:00 on the 11th. No 2026 magusto was found for Faro or Loulé. Portimão's much bigger November fair is in the calendar below.
items.why: Buy a paper cone of hot chestnuts from a street cart and drink a glass of young red with them.

items.name: Festival da Batata-Doce, Aljezur, 28–30 November
items.teaser: Three days for the Lira sweet potato of Aljezur, IGP since 2009, with chefs cooking live
items.story: Aljezur grows its sweet potato, the Lira variety, in the sandy soils of the Costa Vicentina, and it has held a protected geographical indication since 2009. The festival's official site lists the 2026 programme for 28, 29 and 30 November at the Espaço Multiusos de Aljezur. It is about 1h20 west of Faro.

items.name: Clocks back, then All Saints
items.teaser: Clocks go back an hour early on Sun 25 Oct; Sun 1 Nov, All Saints, is a public holiday
items.story: Mainland Portugal follows the European clock change: at 02:00 on Sunday 25 October 2026 the clocks go back to 01:00, and Faro returns to Western European Time, the same as London. Evenings shorten fast; by mid-November the sun sets around 17:20. All Saints' Day, Sunday 1 November, is a national holiday, when families take flowers to the cemeteries. It falls on a Sunday this year, so the effect on opening hours is small. The next holidays are Tuesday 1 December, Restoration of Independence, and Tuesday 8 December, the Immaculate Conception.
items.why: Book sunset drinks for about 17:00 from November, and provision before the 1 and 8 December holidays.
facts: Sun 25 Oct; Sun 1 Nov; Tue 1 Dec; Tue 8 Dec 2026

items.teaser: Portimão's oldest popular event, held each November since 1662: ten days of rides, tasquinhas, chestnuts
items.story: Portimão has held a fair around St Martin's Day since 1662, and the council calls it the town's oldest popular event. The municipal page gives the 2026 dates as 6 to 15 November, at the Parque de Feiras e Exposições, with free entry. Expect fairground rides, tasquinhas, roast chestnuts, farturas and other petiscos, and a crowd: more than 100,000 visitors were reported at a recent edition. The edition number for 2026 could not be confirmed. Portimão is about an hour west of Faro by road, and the fair is a short way inland from the river.

Lisbon's marchas on the night of the 12th are the national show, but the Algarve towns hold their own. For eleven nights it serves what the lagoon gives: clams, oysters, cockles, prawns, octopus and grilled fish, with live music from local and regional bands, from 19:00 to 01:00. bougie.title: 1966 — The year the Barril tuna trap went quiet
bougie.desc: How the Algarve caught the bluefin on its run past the coast, canned it in Vila Real and Olhão, and what is left on the beach at Barril.
bougie.lede: For centuries the Algarve set walls of net across the bluefin tuna's path as it ran along the coast to spawn. At Praia do Barril, near Tavira, the Armação dos Três Irmãos worked from 1841 to 1966. Its fishermen's houses still stand behind the dunes, and some 250 anchors lie in the sand where they were left.
paras: The armação, called almadraba in Spain, is a fixed trap: a long net wall moored by anchors that steered the passing tuna into a chain of chambers, where the fish were hauled up by hand. Sources trace it to Phoenician and Carthaginian settlers, with fixed traps worked under Arab rule. A royal order of 1499 told Lagos to build salting tanks for 3,000 tuna. Traps lined the coast from Vila Real de Santo António to Aljezur and stayed an important income until the catches collapsed in the 1960s and 1970s.

The trap at Barril, the Armação dos Três Irmãos, worked from 1841 to 1966; its arraial, the fishermen's camp, still stands. Up the lagoon, the Arraial Ferreira Neto at Tavira was designed by the engineer Sena Lino in 1943 and opened about 1945. Its archive records the last tuna caught there in 1972, so Barril and Ferreira Neto both claim the last trap. The camp is now a hotel with a small tuna-fishing museum. In 2026 a modern operator, Real Atunara, reported bluefin captures off Barril again.

Tuna also built an industry. In Vila Real de Santo António, founded in 1774, the Andalusian Sebastián Ramirez began in 1853 what his family calls Portugal's first cannery; it moved to Matosinhos in the 1940s. A local writer credits the Genoese Ângelo Parodi with the first tuna-in-oil factory there, the Santa Maria. RTP counted about 200 Algarve canneries in the 1940s and three survivors; Olhão once had 37. Conserveira do Sul, founded there in 1950 or 1954, still cans fish; Portimão's museum fills the old Feu Hermanos cannery.

_corrections: Brief prompt 'the Conserveira do Arade museum in Portimão': no such museum was found. The cannery museum in Portimão is the Museu de Portimão, in the former Feu Hermanos cannery (late 19th century; opened May 2008; Council of Europe Museum Prize 2010, not 'European Museum of the Year').

'The last trap at Barril, 1966': the Barril trap (Armação dos Três Irmãos) worked 1841–1966, but the Ferreira Neto archive records the last tuna there in 1972, and Postal calls Ferreira Neto the last traditional armação of the Algarve. The 'last trap' is disputed.
Ferreira Neto dates: designed by Sena Lino in 1943 (Tavira route); LNEC says inaugurated 1945.
Conserveira do Sul founding: 1954 (Barlavento) vs 1950 (Barlavento on the 2021 sale, Postal).

Ramirez as 'first cannery in Portugal' (1853) is the family's own claim, reported by DN and Forbes; a local writer names Parodi's Santa Maria as the first tuna-in-oil factory in Vila Real. Neither was checked against an archive.
Tuna fishing did not end entirely: Real Atunara reported 2026 bluefin captures off the Armação do Barril; this is a modern operation, not the historic trap.

_notes: Verified by WebSearch on 24 Oct 2026 (WebFetch unavailable; facts come from search summaries, not full pages). Feira de Santa Iria 2026: cm-faro.pt and Algarve Atlas give 15–25 Oct; a Postal headline (Aug 2026) gives 20–29 Oct and another 14–23 Oct; the council dates are used, so the fair ends Sun 25 Oct. Festa do Medronho Monchique: no autumn 2026 date found; past editions moved between Nov, Apr and Jul; 2026 'Vamos à Vila' was 29–31 May. Medronho seasons (picking Sep–Nov, distilling Jan–Mar) come from one documentary description and one Caldeirão walk article. Island boats: only Oct 2024 winter data for Olhão–Armona (four daily, last boat ~17:30); no 2026 Culatra, Armona or Animaris/Deserta winter timetable found. Estaminé winter opening unclear (Visit Portugal: daily Apr–Sep, by reservation otherwise; older Postal: daily all year), so it gets no venue_hot line. Sea temperature from travel-climate sites only (18–20C November). Teatro das Figuras dates from the official agenda via search summary.
